subject: AcmeFin evals follow-up: recommended models, dataset format & next steps
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acmefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Intro & discovery - LLM evals for AcmeFin

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to meet you both. Quick recap from our side and the ask: Acme Financial wants to evaluate candidate LLMs for two production use cases (customer support triage and transaction anomaly summary). Primary goals are precision on financial language, low latency for 1–2s SLO, and strong hallucination controls.

I attached a small sample dataset (acme_sample_dataset.csv) with redacted examples. Next steps we'd like from Redwood: recommended model shortlist, suggested prompt sets to test, and concrete eval scoring criteria so we can run the tests on your platform.

Timeline: we hope to run an initial evaluation in the next 10 business days and then decide on a pilot. Security notes: data must remain in our S3 (we can provide a presigned link) and we require encryption-at-rest + audit log access.

Thanks — Sarah
Sarah Liu
Director, AI Product
Acme Financial

----
Attachment: acme_sample_dataset.csv (3 KB, CSV sample)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acmefin.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 17:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intro & discovery - LLM evals for AcmeFin

Great to meet you on the call, Sarah — thanks for the sample and the clear goals. Recap + proposed plan below.

Summary of objectives
- Use case A: customer support triage (intent classification + short resolution suggestion)
- Use case B: transaction anomaly summarization (concise factual summaries, avoid hallucination)
- SLOs: p50 latency target ~800ms, p95 < 2s for 1–2k token-contexts
- Security: run evals on a private workspace; we support S3 ingestion + optional VPC/private deployment for dataset privacy.

Recommended model shortlist to evaluate (initial round)
- Redwood-1.3-small-latency (our low-latency curated variant; good accuracy/latency tradeoff)
- Llama-2-13b-chat (quantized q4o; strong instruction performance)
- Mistral-7B-Instruct (fast and cost-effective for classification tasks)
- Falcon-40B-instruct (if you want highest-quality summarization; heavier but served as a fallback)

Links and resources
- Benchmark & suggested prompt sets: https://redwood.com/benchmarks/acmefin-eval
- Eval guide & dataset spec (attached): redwood_eval_spec.pdf
- Quickstart eval run (console + CLI examples): https://drive.google.com/redwood/acme-eval-guide

Suggested evaluation setup (short version)
1) Dataset: CSV with columns: id, input, expected_output, eval_type, category, notes. We detail the schema in the attached spec.
2) Metrics: exact_match (for discrete labels), ROUGE-L and BLEU for summarization, and embedding_similarity (Cosine) for semantic match. We also recommend a hallucination score using entailment checks (we include a suggested threshold).
3) Run: we'll ingest your S3 sample (presigned link), set up a private eval workspace tied to your account, and run the models in parallel for apples-to-apples metrics.

Security & logistics
- We can run inside a customer-managed VPC or ingest to a private workspace with encrypted S3. Audit logs for all eval runs are available on request.
- Please send an S3 presigned link (or tell us if you prefer direct upload to our secure transfer).

Next steps (action items)
- Sarah: send representative dataset + confirmation on target metrics and any category weights (by Mon 3/1)
- Marissa/Neha: provision private eval workspace and share CLI run template + expected run time (ETA 24–48h after data receipt)
- Dylan: prepare comparative latency profile for Redwood-1.3 vs Llama-2-13b for Acme sample

I'll attach the detailed eval spec and a short checklist. Happy to hop on a follow-up if you'd prefer a walkthrough.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-1212

----
Attachments: redwood_eval_spec.pdf (12 pages), redwood_benchmark_links.txt (1 KB)

Thanks, Marissa — this is exactly the level of detail we need. A few quick clarifying Qs before we send the full dataset: 

1) Scoring: for the anomaly summaries we care most about factuality and omission (i.e., don't miss key fields). For that, would you recommend a weighted metric that combines ROUGE-L + entailment-based factuality? If so, what default weights do you use?

2) Data redaction/anonymization: our legal team prefers we strip PII. Does Redwood support mapping transformations during ingestion (e.g., token replacement) while preserving the structure for evaluation?

3) Timeline: if we send 2k sample rows by EOB Mon 3/1, what's a realistic ETA for a first-pass report?

Appreciate it — Sarah

Subject: Re: Intro & discovery - LLM evals for AcmeFin

Thanks for the questions — answers below and concrete examples you can hand to legal/engineering.

1) Scoring & recommended weights
- For anomaly summaries we recommend a combined score: 0.5 * ROUGE-L + 0.3 * entailment_score + 0.2 * embedding_similarity.
- ROUGE-L captures recall of key phrases; entailment_score uses a lightweight NLI check against the source fields to penalize hallucinations; embedding_similarity checks semantic closeness to human reference.
- Default pass threshold: combined_score >= 0.80 for pilot acceptance; we can tune by category (e.g., higher threshold for high-risk transaction types).

2) Redaction / transformations during ingestion
- Yes — Redwood's ingestion supports deterministic token replacement (e.g., replace names/accounts with <NAME_1>, <ACCOUNT_123>) and column-preserving hashing. Transformations run client-side if required (we provide a small lambda you can run in your environment) or server-side inside a private workspace. We log the transformation step and provide the mapping if you opt to keep it.

3) ETA / run time
- If you send 2k rows by EOB Mon 2027-03-01: we will provision the workspace within 24h, run the initial eval across the 3 shortlisted models in parallel, and deliver a first-pass report within 48–72h after data receipt (includes latency profile + metric breakdown).

Quick dataset format example (CSV header + row sample)
- Header: id,input,expected_output,eval_type,category,notes
- Sample row: 1001,"Customer: 'My payment didn't go through' -> Last 4 digits: 1234","label:payment_issue","classification","payments","redacted"

CLI quickstart (example)
- redwood evals create-workspace --name acmefin-pilot --private --region us-west-2
- redwood evals ingest --workspace acmefin-pilot --s3-presigned-url "<presigned_url>" --transformations transform_spec.json
- redwood evals run --workspace acmefin-pilot --dataset acme_sample_dataset.csv --models redwood-1.3-small-latency,llama-2-13b-chat,mistral-7b-instruct --metrics exact_match,rouge_l,entailment,embedding_similarity --output report_acmefin.csv

If helpful, Neha can set up the workspace once you share a presigned URL and confirm whether you want transformations applied client-side. Dylan will include a short latency matrix in the report.

Would you like a synchronous walkthrough on Monday? We have a 30-min slot at 11am PT — happy to block it.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

----
Attachments: redwood_eval_spec.pdf (12 pages)
